text:
Sara: Heads up — since ~11:02 UTC we've been seeing a ~35-45% throughput drop on cluster infer-a. Multiple worker restarts and a handful of GPU OOMs reported from nodes a3,a4. Putting initial logs here.
InfraBot: [alert] node infer-a-3 restarted x2, infer-a-4 restarted x1 (11:03 UTC). Rolling restart recommended if instability persists.
Joel: Can you paste the runtime logs and a quick nvidia-smi snapshot? Also pmap of the process would help.
Sara: runtime excerpt below (truncated):
```
[11:02:12] ERROR runtime/allocator: alloc failed size=134217728 ctx=kv_cache tmp_alloc=1
[11:02:13] WARN runtime/serving: eviction spike: evicted=3200 shards, hits=3.8%
[11:02:14] CRIT runtime/worker: OOM when allocating 256MB, restarting worker
```
Joel: thanks. grabbing nvidia-smi and pmap now.
Marco: Profiling snapshot from 11:01-11:03 shows two correlated signals: 1) kernel_selector chose fallback matmul kernel (slower, higher transient memory) at the start of the spike; 2) KV cache eviction rate oscillates every ~2s — eviction bursts line up with allocator failures.
Anika: That eviction oscillation looks like cache thrash. Hit rate drops sharply -> mass evictions -> heavy allocator churn -> fragmentation -> OOMs and restarts. Also batch histogram during the window is skewed to tiny batches (median=1).
Li: FYI we rolled runtime v1.18.5 last night which changed the kernel selection heuristic to prefer the new int8 fallback for some shapes. That fallback allocates larger scratch during setup; combined with high eviction churn this could push us over the edge.
Emma: Immediate mitigations we should try now:
- Set KV_CACHE_MAX_SHARDS=256 for pool infer-a to reduce eviction frequency.
- Temporarily cap max_batch_tokens to 2048 for this pool to limit transient memory spikes.
- Apply tenant-level rate-limit to noisy-tenant svc-x which is sending a lot of tiny prefix-probing requests.
- Rolling restart workers with --graceful to allow allocator to reset without hard OOM loops.
Joel: pasted pmap + nvidia-smi output:
```
# pmap -x pid
00000000004a0000  1024K r--  /opt/runtime/lib/kernel_fallback.so
...
heap     12345678K total,  456K free,  fragmentation_ratio=0.56
# nvidia-smi topo -m
GPU Memory Utilization spike around 11:02, 11:03.
```
Marco: Allocator stats show slab_alloc_failures incrementing right before worker restarts. Free lists dominated by many small free slabs instead of contiguous blocks — classic fragmentation.
Anika: Also observed traffic pattern: svc-x does frequent short prefix requests (median tokens=12) which prevents KV cache from stabilizing and causes repeated cold fills. That amplifies eviction.
Sara: Good context. Proposed action plan:
- Li: revert kernel-selector change for pool infer-a (or force older selector) — rollback candidate for v1.18.5 behavior.
- Emma: apply KV_CACHE_MAX_SHARDS=256 and max_batch_tokens=2048 to pool infer-a; enable tenant rate-limit for svc-x.
- Joel: coordinate graceful rolling restarts of workers in infer-a at low traffic periods.
- Marco: add short-term telemetry: emit kernel_choice and slab_frag_ratio at 60s granularity to cloud metrics.
- Anika: throttle svc-x by 30% and monitor hit rate.
InfraBot: Scheduled rolling restarts for pool infer-a starting 11:40 UTC if config changes applied.
Li: I'll push a selector flag to force old behavior for the pool and add a follow-up PR to adjust heuristics. Also adding a debug metric for scratch_alloc_bytes.
Emma: I'll patch the pool configs now and start rate-limiting svc-x.
Sara: Thanks — I'll own monitoring and canary validation. Will post a follow-up thread in 30m with metrics.
Marco: long-term we should: 1) add an allocator defragmentation pass on low-load windows, 2) revisit kernel fallback memory footprint, 3) improve KV shard autosizing heuristics based on request size distribution.
Anika: Agreed. Also let's add an alert rule for eviction_rate > 5000/min AND slab_frag_ratio > 0.4 to catch this earlier.
Sara: TL;DR: eviction oscillation + new kernel fallback + tiny-batch traffic = allocator fragmentation -> OOM -> restarts. Mitigations applied, monitoring in progress.
Emma: Patch applied and rate-limit enabled. Observing a quick recovery in eviction rate.
Joel: rolling restart started (graceful) at 11:41 UTC.
InfraBot: Note: incident annotated, follow-up required for runtime selector change.
Sara: Follow-up scheduled at 12:10 UTC. Thanks team :thumbsup:
